original: Which trial produces the smallest final volume of gas?
revised_question: Which trial has collected the smallest volume of gas at 60 s?
explanation: Trial B has collected 30 cm³ at 60 s, less than any other trial.

original: Which two trials end with the same total gas volume?
revised_question: Which two trials have collected the same volume of gas by 60 s?
explanation: Trials A and C have both collected 36 cm³ at 60 s.

original: Which trial takes the longest time to stop producing gas?
revised_question: Which trial is still producing additional gas between 50 s and 60 s?
explanation: Trial C rises from 34 to 36 cm³, while the other three curves are horizontal in this interval.

original: A student wants the highest total amount of gas, regardless of speed. Which trial should be chosen?
revised_question: A student wants the greatest amount of gas collected within 60 s. Which trial should be chosen?
explanation: Trial D has collected the largest volume at 60 s: 40 cm³.

original: If Trial C and Trial A have the same final volume but Trial C reaches it sooner, what is the best conclusion?
revised_question: Two other trials produce the same final gas volume. Trial X reaches this volume before Trial Y. What can be concluded?
options: Trial X has a greater average rate over the full reaction
Trial X must have used less reactant
Trial Y must have been hotter throughout
Trial Y must have produced a different gas
explanation: For the same volume, a shorter reaction time gives a greater average rate.

original: Two groups obtain the same final gas volume, but one group starts timing 5 seconds late. How will their graph compare?
revised_question: Two groups start identical reactions together. One starts its stopwatch 5 s late. What error occurs when they record the volume at a stopwatch reading of 10 s?
options: It is actually the volume at 15 s after mixing
It is actually the volume at 5 s after mixing
It must equal the final volume
It proves the reaction is endothermic
explanation: The recorded time is 5 s too small: 10 s on the late stopwatch corresponds to 15 s after mixing.

original: Compared with large chips, how does using powder affect the time to collect 40 cm³ of gas?
revised_question: Compared with large chips, how does using powder affect the time to collect 40 cm³ of gas?
options: It reduces the time by about 71%
explanation: The time falls from 96 s to 28 s. The percentage decrease is (96 − 28) ÷ 96 × 100 ≈ 71%.

original: Between which two temperatures is the greatest drop in reaction time shown?
revised_question: Between which two temperatures is the greatest drop in reaction time shown?
explanation: The greatest fall is from 120 s to 88 s between 20 °C and 25 °C (32 s).

original: Using the graph, estimate the reaction time at 32 °C as ____ s.
revised_question: Using straight-line interpolation between 30 °C (63 s) and 35 °C (44 s), estimate the reaction time at 32 °C. Round to the nearest whole second. ____ s.
